reasons: Correctly identified as a missing-clause deviation: Section 10 addresses access cut-off, Deliverables and refunds only, and 16.5 defers Customer Data to other sections that contain no return/export/deletion duty, so a hosted-services agreement lacks any exit or data-return obligation.

Inserted Section 10.3 tracks the preferred position closely — up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter — and is added as a new subsection without altering existing 10.1/10.2 text (smallest edit that reaches the position).

The backups/legal-retention carve-out on deletion is consistent with the standard already accepted in Section 16.5, so it does not weaken the customer's position materially; the added 'within thirty days of Customer's request' trigger is a minor, defensible variation given clause (a) is also request-based.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, explains the gap and the change, and offers the playbook fallback (ninety days' assistance with the thirty-day export and deletion certificate retained).
